chunks: Muhammad ibn Hammam narrated to us, saying: Humeed ibn Ziyad narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Suma'a narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Maythami narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from his father, who said:

I entered upon Abu Abdillah and asked him about the master of the command after him, so he said to me: 'He is the master of the lamb.' And Musa was in a corner of the house as a boy, and with him was a Mekki lamb, and he was saying to it: 'Prostrate to Allah, Who created you!'
ai.seo_question: Who is the 'master of the lamb' in the hadith of Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the concept of *al-Bahima* (the dumb beast/lamb) as a title for Imam Musa al-Kazim (as), linking his imamate to a miraculous sign observed by the narrator. The scene underscores the transition of authority within the Ahl al-Bayt, where the young Musa demonstrates divine favor through his command to the lamb, a motif often associated with prophetic authority in Shia exegesis. This event serves as a crucial proof (*hujjah*) for the immediate succession of Musa after his father, Imam al-Sadiq (as).
